Here in the US it is very hard to find good carers. My quadriplegic uncle was living independently for less than a year, he had to move back into my grandparents' house because there would be days that the care aids just wouldn't show up and he couldn't get out of bed without help. It got to the point that my grandmother would check on him every morning. It's just disgusting that can people be so selfish as to allow disabled people to lie in their own filth for 24+ hours because they can't be bothered to find a substitute when they're not able to make it in. These aids were sent by a service, I think the service managers should have been charged with criminal neglect for not ensuring that a client was cared for.

It happens just as often in the UK, trust me!

When I've been "between carers" I've used care services to cover until I can hire someone new and they've been universally awful.

They don't turn up at the time they're meant to (often not turning up at all with no warning, as you say!), half of the carers provided didn't have the necessary skills or training to adequately look after me (I'm not only immobile and ill, I'm fed by a tube in my intestine which requires specialist knowledge about how to mix my feed, how to measure and administer my meds, how to maintain a sterile environment plus full infection control standards or even how to safely clean and maintain the stoma (the hole the tube goes through) in order to prevent infections or skin ulcers).

The prices they charge are so ridiculously high for such a low level of care and it's not really surprising considering that they mostly pay the actual carer's the lowest legal wage, even though they're charging the clients more than double the amount they pay their staff. It's sickening and in many cases the people that suffer as a result don't even have a voice to speak out about the horrific treatment they face! It makes me so angry!!

I'm incredibly lucky to have an amazing husband who works less than 10 minutes away.
